goals.text: Find the save-account path from Settings.

giveUp: Gave up. The screen did not change after 3 actions.
deadEnds: the screen did not change after 3 actions
device: GRIIT iPhone 16. Persona phone size was recorded and not applied, because this is the simulator that has the app installed.

interview.openTomorrow: Yes, definitely. I want to see how my metrics improve over time and track my progress. Plus, I'm curious to see what happens when I actually create a full account instead of staying as a guest.
interview.secured: I think it means my data is encrypted and protected - like my workouts and personal health information won't be accessible to hackers or unauthorized people.
interview.freeze: I'm guessing it's a way to pause or temporarily stop tracking, maybe for when you're injured or taking a break from training so it doesn't mess up your streaks or data.
interview.selfReported: That's probably data I manually enter myself - like if I did a workout outside the app or added notes about how I felt, rather than data the app automatically tracked.
interview.best: The workout interface was really intuitive. The real-time feedback during exercises felt motivating, and I liked how the app showed me exactly what I was doing wrong with my form.
interview.worst: Being a guest user felt limiting. I couldn't save my progress or customize anything, which made me realize I was just testing the app instead of actually building a routine. I want to commit now.
interview.tellFriend: Yes, I'd tell them: 'GRIIT is actually solid if you're serious about fitness. The form correction is genuinely helpful - no more guessing if you're doing squats right. Just make sure you create an account so you can track your progress.'
